title: Noor and the Escarpment
premise: Marguerite Villalobos, estranged from her archaeologist father after a dig that cost her mother's life, is pulled into a rescue expedition when his upriver survey goes silent. Racing a salvage fleet that strips wrecks for profit, she must reach the Escarpment site by the sixth tide, navigating rapids, betrayal within her own crew, and the wilderness's unforgiving memory. At the wreck she finds her father alive but broken, guarding artifacts he believes hold their family's history — and must choose between saving him and saving the evidence of who they were. In the end she loses the artifacts to the river but gains a father who finally sees her as an equal, and a found crew worth calling home.
about_author: Ines Lockridge is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who spent six seasons on remote waterways before trading a paddle for a keyboard. Their fiction blends hard-won survival detail with quiet stories about the families we choose.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Working salvage-adjacent dock jobs to stay near the water, Marguerite learns her father's expedition has gone silent upriver. A ragtag crew — gruff pilot Odile, superstitious deckhand Tam, and her father's old rival Brandt — offers passage if she'll navigate the escarpment channels only she knows. Pride wars with grief; she signs on. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment born of unfinished love.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with interludes of her father's final radio logs. The crew battles rapids and discovers someone has sabotaged their fuel — a traitor feeding their position to the salvage fleet. Tam is nearly lost overboard; Marguerite's quick thinking saves him, binding the crew to her. She uncovers Brandt's secret radio transmissions. Emotional beat: trust tested, found family forged in danger.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Climax. Marguerite confronts Brandt — not a traitor but a man bargaining with the fleet to buy their safe passage. They arrive at the Escarpment as the salvage ship closes in; Marguerite dives the flooded dig alone and finds her father trapped in a collapsing chamber, clutching the artifact crate. With the sixth tide rising, she must abandon the artifacts or lose him. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Forgiven Nothing, Forgotten Less
chapters.summary: Resolution, Marguerite's POV. The fleet takes the wreck's cargo; her father, rescued and humbled, grieves the loss of his life's work. Marguerite shows him the one thing she saved — her mother's field journal, hidden years ago in plain sight. Father and daughter begin again on equal ground, and the crew, now family, points the boat home. Emotional beat: memory outlasting treasure, reconciliation earned.
